gaps.sentence: I will always remember the summer ___ we cycled along the Danube.
gaps.explanation: 'When' relates to a time expression like 'the summer'.

gaps.sentence: The 1990s was the decade ___ mobile phones became common.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'in which' after time nouns; 'which' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: The candidate ___ speech impressed us most got the job.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose speech' — the speech belonged to the candidate.

gaps.sentence: All ___ I want is a quiet weekend at home.
gaps.explanation: After 'all' the relative pronoun is 'that' (often omitted); 'all what' is always wrong.
'What caused the fire' means 'the thing that caused it'; 'that' cannot act as the subject of this nominal clause.

gaps.sentence: There is nothing ___ I would change about the design.
gaps.explanation: After 'nothing', use 'that' (or omit the pronoun); 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: The reason ___ he resigned was never explained.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' is the fixed pattern.
